newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Gehe launches new Lloyds bid.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Gehe launches new Lloyds bid.

text.p: A long-running corporate battle for control of Britain's Lloyds Chemists Plc flared anew on Tuesday when German pharmaceutical wholesaler Gehe AG launched a fresh 650.6 million pound ($1.08 billion) bid.

A verbal war between Gehe and its British rival for Lloyds, UniChem Plc, which has raged since both groups first launched takeover bids early this year, heated up as they traded blows in an attempt to win over Lloyds shareholders.

Lloyds responded to the latest Gehe bid by advising its shareholders to take no action. UniChem said it believed that Gehe could obtain less value from Lloyds Chemists in cost savings and revenue benefits than UniChem.

"The shadow boxing period is over. I am confident that when it comes to the line that Lloyds' investors will be interested in taking a stake in an integrated business like ours in the healthcare sector," UniChem chief executive Jeffery Harris said in a telephone interview.

Both Gehe's original bid, an all-cash offer pitched at 500p a share, along with a rival offer from UniChem, lapsed in March after being referred to Britain's competition authority, the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
Unichem, which already owns 9.9 percent of Lloyds, launched another bid on October 18 on the same terms as its offer that lapsed in March.
It is offering 16 new UniChem shares and 926p in cash for every 10 Lloyds shares, valuing Lloyds at 657.6 million pounds.
This time around Gehe, Europe's largest drug distributor, is offering 500 pence in cash for each share in Lloyds and 322.6p in cash for each preference share.
Gehe chairman Dieter Kammerer said in a statement: "This is a highly attractive offer because unlike Unichem's bid it is all cash and is therefore risk-free for Lloyds' shareholders."

UniChem's Harris responded by saying: "I think there is an appetite for shares rather than cash in the London market generally at the moment. So I don't believe that is going to be a factor that weighs in their favour, quite the contrary."

"I don't think his (Kammerer's) management team is as good as ours and that is the reason he has underperformed us in the wholesaling business, in terms of operating margins, ever since I have been in this business," added Harris.
The British government has ruled that if either Unichem or Gehe are successful in acquiring Lloyds, they must sell off specified pats of the business within three months.
Shares in Lloyds Chemists were down 5p at 511-1/2 by 1530 GMT while UniChem shares were 3p higher at 254 pence. In Frankfurt Gehe shares were down 0.50 marks at 101.50 marks. ($1=.6051 Pound)
